seen_animation: A single light bulb drawn in black lines (lopsided round globe, a bent filament line, three slanted thread bands at the base) stands centered on a grey horizontal shelf line, with a grey vase at upper left and a grey picture frame and shelf lines at upper right. In frames 1-4 the bulb is large and its top is cut off by the frame edge. From frame 5 to frame 9 the bulb gets smaller step by step and the grey scenery slides down into view, as if the camera pulls back. From frame 9 to 16 the bulb holds still at the same size and place. In frame 11 short tick marks appear around the neck of the bulb; in frames 12-16 these become longer radiating lines that spread outward and downward from the base, longest in frames 15-16, showing the bulb lighting up.
seen_film: A large frosted light bulb with a brass screw base stands on a dark shelf. In frames 1-3 a small grey-haired old man in a dark cloak peeks out from behind the left side of the bulb and pulls back behind it; by frame 4 only a dark sliver of his cloak shows at the lower left, fading out through frames 5-6. Over frames 1-8 the camera pulls back so the bulb gets smaller and the shelf and background objects (a pale box at upper right, small items at upper left) come into view, with the largest size step between frames 4 and 5. From frame 8 to 16 the bulb holds still. From about frame 13 a soft glow begins around the base, and in frames 14-16 visible light rays fan out from the bottom of the bulb.
named_subject: A hand-drawn light bulb (globe, filament line, three-band screw base).
evidence: Frames 1-4: bulb drawn large with top cropped, matching film frames 1-4. Frame 4 to 5: size drop that matches the film's own size step between frames 4 and 5. Frames 5-9: gradual shrink with the grey vase and frame sliding down, matching the film's pull-back through frame 8. Frames 9-16: bulb held still at a fixed size and place, matching film frames 8-16. Frames 11-16: radiating lines grow from small ticks to long rays around the base, matching the light fan in film frames 14-16, though they start about two frames earlier. In every frame the bulb keeps the doodle's lopsided globe, the bent filament stroke, and the three slanted base bands of c.png. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The light rays begin in frame 11, about two to three frames before the film's glow appears (frame 13 faint, frame 14 clear), so the lighting-up reads early.
closes_when: Frames 11-12 show no ray marks, frame 13 shows only a few short ticks at the base, and the rays lengthen through frames 14-16.
protect: The doodle's exact bulb construction (angular lopsided globe, single bent filament line, three slanted thread bands); the pull-back timing including the size step between frames 4 and 5; the hold from frame 9 on; the rays growing outward gradually from the base rather than popping in; the sparse grey scenery that slides with the camera.
identity_gap: None of consequence: the bulb is the c.png drawing with its own stroke habits, only scaled; the film's peeking old man in frames 1-3 is not part of the doodle and is left out.
